verdict.rationale: Outlook's own inbox rules, categories, search folders and message importance give a way to route and group incoming mail into separate folders or views. However, the evidence comes only from Graph API docs framed as app capabilities. Nothing shows a built-in split inbox or automatic classification into important, team, newsletter and calendar-invite streams that drives priority-ordered triage. Missing for 10: built-in automatic stream classification (important/team/newsletters/invites), user-facing split-inbox UI documentation, evidence of priority-ordered triage, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can split my inbox into focused streams — important, team, newsletters, calendar invites — so triage happens in priority order, not arrival order

citations.quote: Apps can set up [Inbox rules](/en-us/graph/api/resources/messagerule) to promptly handle incoming messages and reduce email clutter.
